text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** Several of the guides I found agree on this.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-4,000 cycles to 80% capacity. The NMC models compared were rated 500-800. In one same-maker pair, the Goal Zero Yeti 1500X (NMC) is rated 500 cycles and the LFP Yeti 1500 is rated 4,000 ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). With daily use, that is roughly 1.4-2 years versus 8-11 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently when they failed. They are not fireproof, and one study found LFP reached thermal runaway sooner under overcharge ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Price:** One retailer-comparison site found a median of $0.55 per Wh for LFP versus $0.95 for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Most new mid-size and large stations are LFP.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per pound, but finished stations narrow the gap a lot. One database found only about a 10% difference at the station level. The SOLIX C1000 (LFP) was even lighter per Wh than the NMC Yeti 1000 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Some of the guides' own numbers disagree with each other, so compare specific models.

**Cold weather**
Chemistry matters less than you'd expect. Most stations of either type refuse to charge below 32°F, so check the manual for the specific unit ([Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Rules of thumb**
- **Daily or frequent use** (van, off-grid, solar): choose LiFePO4.
- **A few outages a year:** either works, since time will age the battery before the cycles run out. Choose on weight and price.
- **If you already own a working NMC unit:** keep using it.
- **Read the cycle claim carefully:** "3,000 cycles to 80%" is a stronger promise than "4,000 to 70%".

**Checking the chemistry before you buy**
Look for "LiFePO4" or "LFP" on the spec sheet, because some makers don't state it. One listing site flags the ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro as NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)), so don't assume.
